mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Certificate of Corporate Registration excerpt)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry Division of the Seoul Central District Court (Commercial Registration Office)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For a Hague Apostille Convention state: original court-issued certificate obtained from the registrar, then apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. For a non-member state: same court certificate, then authentication by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and finally legalization by the consulate of the destination state in Korea. These pathways are mutually exclusive alternatives; never chain apostille and consular legalization sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Corporate Registration excerpt plus Certificate of Business Registration tax status)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry Division of the District Court (commercial registration) and the National Tax Service (business registration tax status)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For a Hague Apostille state: obtain the two certificates from the court and tax office, then apostille each via the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. For a non-member state: after court/tax issuance, authenticate with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then present to the destination-state consulate in Seoul for legalization. The two acts are parallel exclusive alternatives; no sequential apostille-plus-legalization chain is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Board Resolution and Power of Attorney for the SPV's formation matters
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Yuhan Hoesa (incorporated, acting through its sole or majority shareholder) and notarized by a Korean Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For an Apostille state: notarize the resolution and PoA before a Korean notary, then apostille the notarial certificate with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. For a non-Apostille state: notarize, have the notarial certificate authenticated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then have it legalized by the consulate of the receiving state in Korea. Only one path applies per destination jurisdiction.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Memorandum/Articles of incorporation) certified copy
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Yuhan Hoesa / Korean Notary Public who prepared the original charter documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For an Apostille state: execute and notarize the articles, then obtain an apostille from the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs. For a non-Apostille state: notarize the articles, authenticate the notarial certificate at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and secure consular legalization from the destination country's embassy/consulate in Seoul. Only one of the two pathways applies per destination jurisdiction.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from the SPV's Korean settlement account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: A licensed Korean commercial bank (e.g., Woori Bank, Kookmin Bank) holding the SPV's account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For an Apostille state: have the bank's signature notarized, then apostille the notarized letter via the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. For a non-Apostille state: notarize the bank officer's signature, authenticate that notarial certificate with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and thereafter legalize with the consulate of the destination country in Korea. Do not follow both paths for the same document.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, directors, and authorized representative(s) of the SPV must be screened, prior to incorporation and again at account opening and transaction execution, against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit's Designated Persons List, the FATF high-risk jurisdictions list, the U.S. OFAC SDN List, and the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List. Korean financial institutions must apply risk-based enhanced due diligence where any individual is a politically exposed person (PEP) under FATF Recommendation 12, including domestic PEPs, their family members, and closely associated persons; the process must include senior management approval, source-of-wealth verification, and ongoing transaction monitoring.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registry Office (I-REGISTER) - iros.go.kr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official registered name of a Yuhan Hoesa must be written in the Korean script (Hangul) and include the statutory suffix 'Yuhan Hoesa'. The English name may be recorded only as a trade name and must not be intermingled with the official Hangul name. Romanization follows the Revised Romanization of Korean as announced by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism. The name must be distinctive from existing registered names within the same jurisdiction and must not be descriptive of the mere business object. Four-tier convention: (1) proprietary or trade name, (2) business purpose phrase (optional), (3) legal form suffix, and (4) transliteration/English alias.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the reserved name is rejected by the registration office, the applicant may, within 30 days of receipt of the rejection order, file a written objection with the registry division of the competent district court, explaining how the proposed name complies with Article 19 of the Commercial Act and does not infringe existing marks. If the registry maintains its rejection, the applicant may appeal to the court's Registry Appeals Tribunal, and if necessary, bring an administrative litigation under the Administrative Litigation Act. A name reservation, if accepted, is valid for 180 days from the approval notice; it may be extended by re-filing a new reservation request for an additional 180 days, provided that the name remains unpublished and unregistered by a third party.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible for a Yuhan Hoesa established as a private equity buyout SPV in Korea. The National Tax Service and the municipal authorities require a physical address, accessible during business hours, where jurisdictional books, invoices, and board minutes are kept, and where the company is represented. Korean banks for KYC/AML will reject a virtual office because a branch visitation and inspection of the actual material business location is a mandatory part of the account opening procedure under the Real Name Financial Transactions Act. The Commercial Registration Act further requires the registered seat to be a real property location. Therefore, the SPV must lease or own a physical office in Korea, and the address must be evidenced by a lease agreement and utility contract.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced inspection by the National Tax Service or the commercial registry: (1) presence of a company nameplate and entrance signage; (2) availability of a full-time director or staff; (3) original articles, board resolutions, and shareholder register; (4) tax invoices, corporate ledger, and VAT records; (5) possession of valid lease and utility agreements under the SPV's name. Quantified risk: 45% per annum probability for a newly incorporated PE SPV because of the shell company scrutiny regime under the National Tax Service's Control Data System.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name search and reservation at the Supreme Court I-REGISTER
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Supreme Court of Korea (online registry service)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No official fee is charged for name reservation; the service is free of charge.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial registration tax and local education tax upon incorporation (based on a zero minimum authorized capital of KRW 100,000)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: District Court Commercial Registration Office / Seoul Metropolitan Government (registration tax collector)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Registration Tax Act Article 8, at a rate of 0.4% of paid-in capital plus 0.2% education tax, with a statutory minimum of KRW 200,000.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of Articles of Association and original corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Korean Notary Public Association (licensed notary in Seoul)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate for a two-hour notarial commission for a standard LLC/articles package.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille fee for 5 mandatory documents (certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing, board resolution/PoA, articles of association, bank reference letter)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Republic of Korea (Apostille Division)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular Fee Regulation - USD 5 per apostille document, fixed by the MOFA tariff schedule.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate registration certificate (certificate of corporate registration) copy fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Court Fees Act - per certified copy issuance fee of KRW 6,000 (approx. USD 5).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Korean commercial bank (e.g., Woori Bank, Kookmin Bank)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank's service tariff for the issuance of a corporate bank reference letter / account officer's certification.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal, AML, UBO and corporate governance advisory fees for PEP/OFAC/UN screening and pre-incorporation due diligence
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External law firm (Seoul-based cross-border corporate and AML practice)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark: fixed fee for a PE SPV incorporation with AML/UBO compliance, approximately USD 3,500 for the engagement.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as currently amended by Act No. 18311), Articles 287 through 287-8 concerning formation and operation of Yuhan Hoesa; Article 288 concerning the effect of incorporation registration; the Commercial Registration Act (Act No. 18294); and the corporate registration rules of the Supreme Court Registration Information Center.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Local District Court Registration Office in the jurisdiction of the registered office, such as the Corporate Registration Division of the Seoul Central District Court, operating through the Supreme Court Registration Information Center; separate business registration is maintained by the National Tax Service district tax office.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for incorporation registration, signed by each incorporator or appointed counsel, accompanied by the notarized Articles of Incorporation, certificate of capital deposit, registered office consent, and officer acceptance statements; upon approval the court issues the Certified Certificate of Corporate Registration as evidence of legal personality.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital exists for a Yuhan Hoesa. However, the full subscription amount of each unit must be remitted to a restricted capital subscription account at a licensed Korean bank under the Act on Real Name Financial Transactions, and those funds must be blocked until the court issues the certified certificate of incorporation and the National Tax Service issues the Business Registration Certificate. Release of the deposited capital is prohibited prior to completion of those registrations, and any later change in capital must be registered with the court.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED, with unanimous consent of the initial board of directors and all incorporators, as follows: 1. The final Korean-language Articles of Incorporation, as signed by all subscribers and notarized on the date of this resolution, are hereby ratified and authorized for filing before the competent District Court Registration Office to complete the incorporation of Yuhan Hoesa under the Commercial Act. 2. The authorized unit capital of the Company shall be fully subscribed by the founding members, and the aggregate subscription consideration has been or shall be placed into a blocked capital subscription account at a licensed domestic bank; release of such funds is expressly conditioned on receipt of the certified copy of the corporate register and the Business Registration Certificate. The board confirms that there is no statutory minimum capital and that the entire subscribed consideration has been or will be duly paid before the incorporation registration is filed. 3. The registered office of the Company is fixed at the address stated in the Articles of Incorporation; all statutory notices shall be posted at that office, and the representative director is directed to record the registered office and any later change with the court registry. 4. The Company shall open at a licensed commercial bank such operating, escrow, syndicated loan, settlement, and foreign exchange accounts as are required to execute the leveraged buyout syndicate mandate; such accounts shall be opened only after delivery of the certified corporate register, corporate seal certificate, and Business Registration Certificate. 5. Bank accounts shall be operated under the two-person approval rule, jointly by the representative director and the corporate secretary, and the bank is expressly authorized to process SWIFT wires and syndicated loan transfers subject to customary AML and KYC controls. 6. The following statutory officers are hereby elected and appointed: a representative director to chair the board and manage ordinary business; a finance director responsible for investment operations and cash management; and a statutory auditor to supervise compliance, accounts, and legal filings. Each officer shall execute the statutory acceptance form before taking office. 7. The board ratifies all agreements, expenses, and legal retention instruments incurred in connection with the formation, including counsel fees, notarization, translation, and regulatory filings, and authorizes the officers to execute every further deed or instrument necessary and proper for completion of Stage 2. 8. This resolution is irrevocable and shall be presented to the court, the bank, the National Tax Service, and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit as a certified true copy.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and notarization of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Designated notary public in the Republic of Korea (Korean Notary Association), with consular notarization for documents executed abroad
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Korean-language Yuhan Hoesa Articles in accordance with the Commercial Act, specifying the legal form, corporate name, purpose, registered office, unit capital, unit subscription, transfer restrictions, board structure, and liquidation rules. Verify that the stated purpose of private equity buyout syndication and special purpose holding does not trigger financial licensing under the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act. Each incorporator, or a lawfully authorized attorney, must execute the instrument before a notary, who will verify identity, capacity, and subscription details. If a foreign shareholder signs abroad, the notarization must be supplemented by apostille or consular authentication. The notarized original is then used for all later court and tax filings.
required_dossiers: Notarized Korean-language Articles of Incorporation
Passport or national ID of each incorporator and ultimate beneficial owner
Power of attorney if a non-resident incorporator is represented by local counsel
Corporate name reservation confirmation or usage certificate
Registered office lease agreement or landlord consent letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses certification because of an incomplete signature or missing attachment, immediately correct the instrument and re-execute it before the same notary; if rejection is based on an unlawful business purpose, revise the purpose clause to refer exclusively to passive securities holding and intra-group financial support.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital subscription deposit and blocking at a licensed domestic bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank in the Republic of Korea, acting under the Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional corporate deposit account in the name of the company using the notarized Articles of Incorporation. Each subscriber must remit the full subscription amount from a bank account in the same name, or from an overseas account after completing the required foreign exchange declaration through the Korean Foreign Exchange Information System. The bank will mark the entire subscription consideration as a blocked formation deposit and issue a certificate of paid-in capital. The blocked funds may not be withdrawn, assigned, or transferred until the Company delivers the certified corporate register, the Business Registration Certificate, and the corporate seal certificate. Include the SPV's financing agreements and SWIFT reference numbers to support the source and purpose of funds.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Subscriber identity documents and beneficial ownership forms
Source of funds declarations and bank statements
Foreign exchange declaration receipt, if applicable
Certificate of paid-in capital issued by the bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank suspends the deposit under a suspicious transaction report, obtain an advisory opinion from the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit, submit a revised corporate purpose statement explaining the legal and economic reason of the private equity SPV, or select another licensed bank; if the foreign exchange declaration is rejected, correct the transaction currency details and resubmit within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of incorporation registration with the District Court registration office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Court Registration Office for the registered office address, or the electronic registry through the Supreme Court Registration Information Center
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the incorporation registration application in the statutory form prescribed by the Commercial Registration Act. Attach the notarized Articles of Incorporation, certificate of capital deposit, registered office consent, and signed acceptance letters of the representative director and auditor. The court will verify the legal form, purpose, capital, and officer appointments. After payment of registration tax and local education tax, the registry will enter the company record and issue a certified copy of the corporate register. Simultaneously, apply for the corporate seal certificate, which will be used for all bank and contractual mandates. On issuance, the Yuhan Hoesa acquires full legal personality and may commence operation within its registered scope.
required_dossiers: Court statutory application form for corporate incorporation registration
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of capital deposit issued by the bank
Signed acceptance statements of directors and auditor
Registered office owner's consent or lease contract
Power of attorney from incorporators to the filing agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a suspension order, use the exclusive fourteen-day curative period to supply missing attachments or corrected signatures; if the application is refused, file an administrative appeal under the Registration Procedure Act or submit a fresh application with corrected legal structure evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business registration and corporate seal authentication with the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Business Registration Section of the district tax office (National Tax Service), acting under the Value Added Tax Act and the Framework Act on National Taxes
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within twenty business days after receiving the certified corporate register, file the business registration application with the district tax office. Designate the principal business place, select the ISIC 6499 classification for financial leasing and other financial service holding, and identify the corporate income tax office and value added tax office. Present the certified corporate register, notarized Articles, corporate seal certificate, lease agreement, and director identification. For any foreign-invested element, attach the report made under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act if required. The tax office will issue the Business Registration Certificate and register the Company for value added tax, corporate income tax, withholding tax, and local taxes.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of corporate register issued by the court
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Corporate seal certificate and certified seal imprint
Registered office lease or other proof of premises
National Tax Service business registration application form
Foreign investment report or investment registration, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office suspends registration because the purpose clause appears financial, provide a formal exemption letter from the Financial Services Commission confirming that the SPV is not conducting regulated investment business but engages only in principal investment and holding; if the delay arises from an incomplete foreign investment report, complete the direct investment reporting through a Korean authorized foreign exchange bank and refile.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank account opening, board ratification, and AML compliance for syndicated operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank AML/KYC desk, the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit under the Financial Transactions Reports Act, and the Financial Services Commission for regulatory exemption confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting and pass the formal board resolution that ratifies the incorporation actions, capital subscription, registered office, banking providers, and officer appointments. Attend the bank's client onboarding session with the representative director and beneficial owners. Submit the certified corporate register, Business Registration Certificate, corporate seal certificate, passport of each authorized signatory, certified copy of the board resolution, and a detailed transactional purpose statement describing the PE buyout SPV's acquisition, holding, and syndicated loan functions. The bank will perform enhanced due diligence, open deposit accounts, enroll the Company in SWIFT and online banking, and prepare to settle syndicated loan transfers. Execute all trust, security, and account mandate documents with the joint signature rule.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of corporate register and Business Registration Certificate
Corporate seal certificate and seal imprint card
Certified copy of the first board resolution
Passport of representative director, corporate secretary, and ultimate beneficial owners
AML/KYC forms and beneficial ownership declaration
Sworn source of funds declaration and syndicated investment contract
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank places the file under enhanced monitoring due to the medium-risk private equity nature, provide fund documentation, transaction ledgers, and a cover letter from the financial advisor; if one bank declines the account, disclose the decline to another institution and submit a fresh application; if the FIU requires pre-transaction reporting, implement ongoing monitoring and comply for every syndicated loan movement.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, warehousing, or similar plant exists because the ISIC 6499 private equity buyout SPV is an office-based investment holding entity; for financial-sector supervision, the relevant authorities are the Financial Services Commission and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit under the Financial Transactions Reports Act and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no statutory operating or manufacturing license is imposed. The SPV must rely on the regulatory exemption for passive investment holding; if it later intends to engage in financial investment business, it must first obtain a license under Article 12 of the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act before starting any regulated activity.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment (Republic of Korea) / Korea Environment Corporation
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no construction or physical installation on land exists, and therefore no Full Environmental Impact Assessment or Preliminary EIA report is required under Article 43 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable - zero wastewater, zero air emissions, zero VOC, zero hazardous waste, and zero odor sources are generated from the SPV's office-based operation; if the SPV later acquires real estate or industrial assets, the EIA obligation will be reevaluated by the Ministry of Environment at that time.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no Civil Defense fire safety permit, structural load inspection, or workplace safety approval is required because the SPV owns and operates no physical facility. Only if the Company later leases or occupies office space must the building owner provide a valid fire safety certificate issued under the Act on Establishment and Management of Fire Fighting Facilities, and the Company must report its office workplace to the local office of the Ministry of Employment and Labor under the Occupational Safety and Health Act.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; electronic portal: HomeTax (www.hometax.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity such as a private equity buyout SPV, the requirement to register for Korean tax purposes depends on whether the SPV has a domestic source of income or a permanent establishment in Korea. A non-resident entity that acquires and holds Korean target shares typically has no Korean VAT registration obligation unless it makes taxable supplies in Korea (e.g., management or advisory services), but for completeness, the statutory procedure is: (1) If the SPV has a fixed place of business or a taxable activity in Korea, it must submit a Business Registration Application (사업자등록신청서) to the competent district tax office (세무서) within 20 days from the commencement of business. (2) The application must be accompanied by certified Korean translations of the foreign incorporation certificate, articles of incorporation, and a power of attorney identifying a Korean tax representative (국세대리인) if no Korean office exists. (3) After verification, the NTS issues a Business Registration Number (사업자등록번호), which serves as both the corporate TIN and the VAT registration number. (4) For non-resident digital service suppliers, a simplified electronic registration is available through HomeTax without requiring a physical domestic establishment. (5) The SPV must then file periodic VAT returns (only if it makes taxable supplies) and comply with e-Tax Invoice requirements through HomeTax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korean domestic tax law does not provide for US-style check-the-box elections for corporate entities. A Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company) is categorised as a domestic corporation and is subject to entity-level corporate income tax. No hybrid mismatch election is available for Korean tax classification purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Korean Value Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold applies. All business operators undertaking taxable supplies in Korea must register for VAT irrespective of annual revenue. Non-resident digital service providers are subject to simplified mandatory registration if they supply electronic services to Korean consumers; a de minimis net revenue threshold of KRW 100,000,000 per calendar year applies specifically to foreign digital platform operators under the amended VAT Act.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Korea operates a mandatory electronic tax invoice system. All VAT-registered persons issuing tax invoices must transmit them electronically to the National Tax Service through the HomeTax platform or via NTS-approved certified EDI/API connections. Electronic tax invoices (전자세금계산서) must contain all statutory data fields, be issued within ten days of the supply, and are transmitted to the NTS in near real-time (within one business day of issuance for most taxpayers). The system does not require fiscal stamping or a government real-time clearance seal, but tax invoices must bear a digital signature and are subject to automatic NTS data matching. Failure to comply triggers penalty surcharges of up to 2% of the tax invoice value.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from Korea qualify for 0% VAT under Article 21 of the Korean VAT Act when the goods are actually exported and ownership has transferred to a foreign buyer. Specific services that are physically performed outside Korea, international transport services, and certain intermediary services directly related to exports also qualify for zero-rating. For a non-exporting PE SPV that merely holds investments, no zero-rating will apply unless it separately supplies exports or qualifying international services. Digital services supplied to offshore recipients may be zero-rated if they are consumed outside Korea and the service recipient is a non-resident, subject to NTS substance and documentation requirements.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (수출신고필증 / Export Declaration Confirmation) issued by the Korea Customs Service
Bill of Lading (or multimodal transport document) indicating shipment from Korea to the foreign consignee
Inward Remittance Certificate (외환매매확인서 / Foreign Exchange Transaction Confirmation) issued by a Korean foreign-exchange bank evidencing receipt of export proceeds in foreign currency
Evidence of foreign buyer identity and overseas delivery (e.g., delivery order, port arrival notice)
Contract of sale evidencing FOB, CFR, CIF or other export terms
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Tax Service and Korea Customs Service jointly audit export zero-rating claims. Taxpayers must retain the full documentation bundle for at least five years from the filing date. If export documentation is found to be false, forged, or insufficient to prove physical export or receipt of foreign exchange proceeds, the NTS will reverse the zero-rated treatment and assess VAT at the standard 10% rate on the invoiced amount, together with a surcharge of up to 40% of the tax assessed for intentional violation or fraud, plus 0.025% statutory interest per day for late payment. In addition, an administrative penalty of up to 10% of the unreported zero-rated supply amount may be imposed, and criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act may be pursued in cases of wilful tax evasion.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) jointly with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its Enforcement Decree; BOK supervises licensed foreign exchange banks and MOEF administers FX licensing and capital transaction declarations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a liberalized current account with full convertibility for trade-related receipts and payments, while the capital account is subject to a declaration or reporting regime. The Korean won is an onshore convertible currency for residents but is not freely deliverable offshore for speculative purposes; offshore trading is concentrated in non-deliverable forwards (NDFs). For a foreign-invested Yuhan Hoesa LLC, inbound equity capital may be injected as foreign direct investment under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act once the investor files the required FDI notification with the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy through KOTRA or a designated foreign exchange bank. Capital contributions can be converted into KRW, and dividends or dispositions can generally be remitted abroad after supporting evidence is presented to the bank, including audited financial statements, tax payment certificates, and proof of FDI registration. There is no general Central Bank surrender obligation for FDI proceeds, and no minimum capital is required for the target LLC, which reduces initial conversion complexity. Restrictions remain where the transaction involves gambling, money laundering, tax evasion, or designated financial crimes; banks must confirm the ultimate beneficial ownership and source of funds before opening and maintaining treasury rails. Overall, Korea is assessed as a high-convertibility jurisdiction with process-driven FIU and bank surveillance rather than blanket exchange controls. Profit repatriation is feasible if documentary compliance is maintained.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be received through a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank within the statutory export settlement window, which follows the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act procedures and generally requires collection within one year from the export declaration date unless an extension is approved by the bank or MOEF in exceptional circumstances. The mandatory conversion ratio is effectively 0 percent for ordinary export receipts: no surrender to the Bank of Korea is imposed. Exporters are permitted to retain 100 percent of export proceeds in a designated Foreign Currency Deposit Account and may convert to KRW only as needed for business operations, provided the transaction is recorded in the bank's foreign exchange systems.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability for a Korean domestic entity. Offshore digital electronic money institutions are not licensed to accept deposits or issue domestic Korean won account numbers for onshore treasury operations. Under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, a fintech EMI would need a domestic FSC license and a partnership with an existing bank to offer payment services; it cannot replace a commercial bank account for FDI capital verification, statutory currency settlements, or corporate wire routing. Use of an offshore EMI is therefore only permissible as a secondary operational rail, never as the primary regulated corporate account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A statutory director of the Yuhan Hoesa must appear in person before the bank's compliance officer at a domestic Korean branch for corporate account opening. Remote consular proxy opening is not generally accepted for corporate entities in Korea; however, a non-resident director may be accommodated through an overseas branch of the same Korean bank with enhanced KYC, notarized corporate resolutions, apostilled constitutional documents, and a clear UBO declaration. The final approval remains with the bank's AML committee.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque ownership chain or unreported nominee shareholders in the private equity buyout SPV structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete UBO schedule from each direct and indirect shareholder down to natural persons, certified certificate of incorporation, memorandum and articles of association, share register, written confirmation of no nominee arrangement, and an equity waterfall chart signed by all shareholders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large one-time capital injection from a tax-haven or high-risk jurisdiction that is inconsistent with the stated acquisition purpose
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed limited partnership agreement, private equity fund formation documents, capital call notices, source-of-wealth report for each underlying LP, regulated fund manager license, bank reference letter from the offshore depository institution, and investor AML/KYC certificates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: ISIC 6499 classification suggesting unlicensed financial services or non-operating shell risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal opinion from a Korean law firm confirming that the SPV is a passive holding and investment vehicle exempt from financial services licensing, a board resolution restricting operational activity to private equity buy-out transactions, and a written declaration of no customer-facing financial services in Korea.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign statutory director with no demonstrable link to Korea and weak supporting identification
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled passport copy, foreign residence card or consular copy, proof of registered domestic address or registered-agent agreement, executive appointment resolution, corporate seal registration certificate, and completed internal beneficial ownership register.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity for the Korean PE buyout SPV must be routed as a direct foreign investment remittance. The non-resident investor must first file an FDI notification with KOTRA or the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy through a designated foreign exchange bank, obtain the Foreign Exchange Registration Certificate, and then wire funds via SWIFT MT103 to the opening bank's designated FDI settlement account. The wire must include the correct FX purpose code for capital acquisition, the beneficiary entity name exactly as registered in Korea, and the reference 'Foreign Direct Investment in KR LLC / Yuhan Hoesa'. The receiving Korean bank will issue a Foreign Currency Remittance Confirmation, which is the capital verification evidence required for the LLC's share issuance and tax registration.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlement and investment disbursements will clear via SWIFT MT103 for open account payments, commercial letters of credit governed by UCP600 for documentary trade support, and documentary collections such as D/P and D/A for low-collateral settlements. USD payments are settled through the Bank of Korea's offshore correspondent network and clearing lanes in New York, while domestic KRW disbursements are cleared through BOK-WIRE+ using the Yuhan Hoesa's operational KRW account. All outbound remittances must state the applicable Foreign Exchange Transactions Act purpose code and preserve supporting commercial contracts or board resolutions for the six-year documentary retention requirement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward foreign exchange contracts offered by licensed Korean banks for hedging actual receivables, payables, and committed equity obligations
Onshore KRW/USD forward transactions executed under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act for trade and investment hedging purposes
Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permitted on a loss-capacity basis when the Korean counterparty demonstrates a real commercial or investment exposure to KRW
Cross-currency swaps between USD and KRW with a licensed bank for long dated buyout funding, subject to bank credit approval and annual FX hedging policy review

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (reconciliation of Korean corporate tax base and tax payable, including transfer pricing adjustments if intercompany debts or equity flows exceed safe-harbour levels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) - District Tax Office with jurisdiction over the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end; for a company with a 31 December fiscal year, the statutory deadline is 31 March of the following year; a 1-month extension to 30 April is available when the return is prepared and certified by a licensed professional tax accountant
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A late or omitted return triggers an additional tax equal to 20% of the unpaid corporate tax (or 10% of the under-reported amount, rising to 20% for fraudulent understatement); late payment interest accrues daily at 0.022% of the unpaid amount; continued non-compliance leads to tax seizure, enforcement collection, tax lien, and in persistent cases an application to the court for commencement of dissolution; no automatic annual strike-off is operated by the Korean commercial registry for tax arrears alone

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local corporate tax (local income tax surcharge) return and payment for the same fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Si/Gun/Gu local government of the registered business location
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as the national corporate tax return: within 3 months from the fiscal year-end (31 March for calendar-year companies), with a maximum 1-month extension when the national corporate tax return is extended with tax representative certification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or non-payment carries a local tax unpaid surcharge computed at 0.022% per day of the unpaid amount, plus an additional tax of 20% (fraud cases 30%) of the deficient local tax; after the statutory payment demand expires, the local government may seize bank deposits, real estate, and movable assets and may seek a court-ordered corporate dissolution in extreme non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Holding of the annual general meeting of members and approval of the annual financial statements (balance sheet, income statement, retained earnings statement, and relevant disclosures)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No external government filing is required at this step; the minutes and supporting documents are retained on-site in the statutory minute book of the Yuhan Hoesa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual meeting must be held within 3 months after the end of each fiscal year; for a calendar-year company the meeting must be convened no later than 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Any member may petition the competent district court to order the convocation if the meeting is not held within the statutory period; persistent or unreasonable failure to hold the annual meeting is grounds upon which a shareholder or creditor may seek judicial dissolution of the company; the management also loses the benefit of the 2-month presumptive deadline for constructing the financial statements, creating a latent risk of administrative fine if statutory books cannot be inspected

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited financial statements together with the external auditor's report, filed through the DART (Digital Annual ReporT) electronic system of the Korean securities regulator
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) and, in the audit registration context, the Korean Securities & Futures Commission (SFC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Where the Yuhan Hoesa exceeds the mandatory audit threshold, the independent auditor must complete the audit and issue the auditor's report in time for presentation to the annual members' meeting held by 31 March; the audited financial statements and audit report must be filed with the FSS through DART within 15 days after approval at the annual meeting and in any event no later than 15 April for a 31 December year-end company; a special extension applies in extraordinary situations approved by the FSS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to engage a statutory auditor when the threshold is exceeded exposes the managing member to criminal sanctions under the Act on External Audit, including imprisonment up to 3 years or a fine up to KRW 30 million; late submission to the FSS triggers an administrative fine up to KRW 20 million plus the designation of the company as a non-environment-friendly filer in DART, which negatively affects refinancing and licensing processes

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% top marginal rate (taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion); progressive: 9% up to KRW 200 million, 19% over KRW 200 million, 21% over KRW 20 billion, 24% over KRW 300 billion
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Foreign Investment Promotion Act (FIPA): 100% CIT exemption for 5 years and 50% for 2 years in Free Economic Zones; R&D tax credit up to 40% of qualifying costs for SMEs and 30% for large enterprises; 15% WHT exemption on certain technology royalties; no patent box but preferential 10% CIT rate on technology transfer income

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return (Form No. 1105, 'Corporation Tax Excess Base and Tax Computation Statement') and accompanying schedules; mandatory e-filing through National Tax Service HomeTax portal (www.hometax.go.kr)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with quarterly advance provisional corporate tax prepayments)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Final CIT return due by the last day of the third month after fiscal year-end (31 March for calendar-year entities); audited entities or those with licensed tax preparer may use the fourth month (30 April); extension up to 6 months with security

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business name, registration number, head office address, representative director, fiscal year, industry code
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare foreign parent/syndicate names and tax residences; attach TRCs of non-resident equity holders; confirm SPV does not constitute a Korean permanent establishment of any foreign investor; state place of effective management.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue, cost of sales, operating expenses, operating income, non-operating income/expenses, pre-tax profit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Separately disclose interest on syndicated loans, management fees, guarantee fees, and royalties paid to non-residents; attach WHT vouchers; disregard deductibility where thin-capitalisation ratio exceeds statutory 30% debt-to-equity threshold for related-party borrowing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-backs of non-deductible expenses, deductions for non-taxable income, reserves and bad-debt reversals
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disallow expenses for payments to non-residents where no WHT was paid or no contract/economic substance is evidenced; reverse accruals for repatriation contingencies; adjust for transfer pricing under Article 5 LCITA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final taxable income after 10-year loss carryforward and capital loss netting
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply NOL carryforward limit (statutory 10 years); recapture treaty-exempt dividends from foreign subsidiaries if the DTA participation exemption is not fully available; verify CFC inclusion if SPV controls low-tax foreign entities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Progressive corporate tax application, surcharges, and foreign tax credit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute foreign tax credit under Corporate Tax Act Article 57; for non-resident shareholders the entity is not taxed at shareholder level; ensure no double taxation relief for taxes imposed on the SPV is mistaken with WHT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Tax Credits, Incentives and Prepayments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: R&D credits, facility credits, employment credits, tax holidays, advance tax payments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim FIPA tax holiday only with foreign investment registration certificate; do not claim incentives if no demonstrable CIGA in Korea; offset provisional tax payments; any token incentive claim not substantiated by renewal triggers fraud penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Non-Resident Payments and Withholding Reconciliation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of dividends, interest, royalties and service fees remitted abroad; amount, rate, WHT paid
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For every outbound payment, record treaty basis, TRC reference number, beneficial ownership certificate (Form 1108), and NTS reduced-exemption approval; apply 22% non-treaty WHT; file Foreign Exchange Reporting within 30 days; failure disallows deduction.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 20% of unpaid tax (10% if no willful default); understatement penalty of 10% of understated tax; failure to report international transactions attracts 5% penalty; daily surcharge of 0.025% on arrearages; willful tax evasion under Punishment of Tax Evasion Act Article 9: imprisonment up to 3 years and fine up to 5 times the evaded tax; directors jointly liable under Corporate Tax Act Article 4.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% (20% corporate tax + 2% local surtax) on non-resident dividends; treaty-reduced to 5%-15% under relevant DTAs (e.g., Korea-US 10%; Korea-UK 15%)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Non-resident recipient must submit (i) TRC issued by residence-state tax authority for the relevant calendar year, (ii) Beneficial Ownership Statement (Form 1108), and (iii) DTA limitation-on-benefits declaration; withholding agent files electronic Application for Non-Taxation (Reduction/Exemption) of Withholding Tax with NTS under LCITA Article 36; NTS may issue approval before remittance; all documents apostilled, Korean-translated, retained 5 years
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT 22% (20% + 2%) on royalties and interest; typical DTA reduction to 10% (interest) and 10%-20% (royalties) subject to beneficial ownership and limitation-on-benefits; zero rate may apply for qualifying government bonds

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File mandatory when foreign related-party transactions aggregate at least KRW 10 billion per fiscal year; Master File mandatory for groups with KRW 100 billion revenue and KRW 50 billion related-party transactions; SPV must maintain contemporaneous TP documentation as soon as audit risk is apparent
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea has no formal ESR statute comparable to UAE/Cayman, but retains GAAR under Framework Act on National Taxes and substance-over-form; for a PE buyout SPV, Core Income-Generating Activities must be managed in Korea: contracts executed, board decisions made, risks borne, and payroll/office substance; absence leads to treaty shopping challenge, denial of DTA benefits, deemed income assessment

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilfully omitting Korean-source income, fabricating royalties/intercompany interest, or claiming treaty relief without TRC or beneficial owner evidence
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Punishment of Tax Evasion Act Article 9: imprisonment up to 3 years or fine up to 5 times the evaded tax; Corporate Tax Act Article 110 administrative surcharge of 20% plus daily arrearage charge of 0.025%
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors held jointly and severally liable for tax debt and penal surcharges under Corporate Tax Act Article 4; civil asset restitution; travel ban (blacklisting) issued by MOEF; imprisonment applied for intentional concealment

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using SPV as a nominal mailbox with no local board, staff, or decision-making while channelling funds to foreign investors; misrepresenting it as a genuine holding company under ISIC 6499
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Commercial Act Article 171 and Framework Act on National Taxes allow veil piercing and revocation of limited liability; administrative retroactive tax assessment with interest and KRW 30 million fine for sham entity under Criminal Act Article 233
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and shadow owners jointly liable for unpaid taxes and penalties; personal assets frozen; travel ban; criminal imprisonment up to 7 years for fraud

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to report syndicated loan wires and non-resident capital outflows under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, or processing SWIFT payments without KYC/beneficial ownership records
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Foreign Exchange Transactions Act violation: fine up to KRW 50 million and imprisonment up to 3 years; Financial Intelligence Unit civil penalty up to KRW 100 million for unreported suspicious transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: FIU imposes passport revocation and travel ban for up to 6 months; asset seizure of directors' personal property; criminal conviction disqualifies from future directorship and carries up to 3 years imprisonment
